subject: Biology
title: Producers, Consumers, and Decomposers
description: A 60-second lesson on Producers, Consumers, and Decomposers.

hook.text: Every organism in an ecosystem plays a role: make food, eat food, or break down the dead.

buildup.text: Producers like plants and algae capture sunlight and convert it into chemical energy.

discovery.text: Consumers eat other organisms. Herbivores eat plants; carnivores eat animals; omnivores eat both.

twist.text: Decomposers are the unsung heroes—fungi and bacteria recycle dead matter back into nutrients.

climax.text: Without decomposers, dead material would pile up and nutrients would be locked away forever.

punchline.text: Death feeds life. That's the circle.

quiz.question: What role do decomposers play in an ecosystem?
options: They recycle dead matter into nutrients
They hunt and eat other animals

details.summary: Producers like plants and algae convert light energy into organic matter through photosynthesis. Consumers eat producers or other consumers for energy. Decomposers break down dead organisms, recycling nutrients back into the soil for producers to use again.
details.whyItMatters: These three groups form the foundation of every ecosystem's energy and nutrient flow. Without producers, there is no energy input. Without decomposers, nutrients would remain locked in dead matter and ecosystems would grind to a halt.
takeaways: Producers form the base of every food web by converting sunlight to food
Consumers are classified as herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores
Decomposers recycle nutrients making them available for producers again

faq.question: Why are decomposers so important to ecosystems?
faq.answer: Without decomposers, dead organisms would pile up and nutrients would be permanently locked away. Bacteria and fungi break down organic matter, releasing nitrogen, phosphorus, and carbon back into the soil and atmosphere where producers can use them again.

faq.question: Are all producers plants?
faq.answer: No. Algae, cyanobacteria, and some protists are major producers in aquatic ecosystems. Chemosynthetic bacteria around hydrothermal vents produce organic matter from chemical energy without sunlight. In the ocean, phytoplankton produce half of global oxygen.
